scalars.scalar_value: A bachelor’s degree from a recognized college or university in public administration, business administration, human resources, law, education, disability studies, or a related field AND two years of experience coordinating compliance, programs, or projects of comparable complexity.

items.item_text: 01. Candidates who are successful in this examination process may be contacted for future employment opportunities (within this classification) that may be at a different site than where the current vacancy is located. Which locations within VCCCD are you willing to work? (Check all that apply.) You will only be considered for vacancies at locations at which you indicate you are willing to work in response to this question. Options: District Administrative Center (Located in Camarillo) | Moorpark College | Oxnard College | Ventura College

02. Please indicate the type of job (fulltime and/or part-time) AND the type of work (regular and/or temporary) that you are willing to accept. (Check all that apply). You will only be considered for vacancies with the type of job AND work that you are willing to accept. Options: Fulltime Job | Part-Time Job | Regular/Permanent Work | Temporary Work

03. PLEASE READ THE FOLLOWING STATEMENT: Answer the following questions as truthfully and accurately as possible. You are not expected to answer at the highest level of each of these items to be qualified. The application will be evaluated for minimum qualifications. Your responses to the supplemental questions below may also be used to determine your qualifications beyond the minimum qualification requirements for this classification in a training and experience (T&E) evaluation. Referring to your application/resume, listing "see resume", or incomplete responses will NOT qualify as a response to any question. Questions that are answered in this method will be considered INCOMPLETE and may result in DISQUALIFICATION. You are required to answer ALL of the supplemental questions as truthfully and accurately as possible. Your responses to these questions are subject to verification and may be assessed in subsequent examination parts. All experience, education, training, and certification must be included in your application in order to be considered. Any sign of deliberate misinformation or intentional exaggeration will result in disqualification from this examination process and possible bar from future employment opportunities with the Ventura County Community College District (VCCCD). Select "Yes" if you have read, understood, and agree to the above statements. Select "No" if you have read, understood, and DO NOT agree with the above statements and voluntarily withdraw your application for this position. Options: Yes | No

04. Which of the following best describes the highest level of education you have successfully completed? Options: High School Diploma or educational equivalent | Associate's Degree | Bachelor's Degree from a recognized college or university in public administration, business administration, human resources, law, education, disability studies, or a related field. | Master's Degree or higher from a recognized college or university in public administration, business administration, human resources, law, education, disability studies, or a related field. | Bachelor's degree in an unrelated field | Master's degree or higher in an unrelated field
05. What is your bachelor's major and/or your master's degree major? If you have both degrees, please list the majors of each diploma.

06. Describe any specialized coursework, certifications, or professional training related to ADA, accessibility, disability services, compliance, law, human resources, education, or related field. If you have not completed any such coursework, mark N/A. Note: This experience must be noted in your application to be considered.

07. How many years of experience do you have coordinating compliance programs, or projects of comparable complexity. Options: No Experience | Less than six months | At least six months but less than one year | At least one year but less than two years | Two or more years

08. Describe your experience coordinating compliance programs or projects. In your response, indicate (a) the organization(s) where you gained this experience, (b) the dates of employment, and (c) provide a summary of the compliance programs or projects that you coordinated. If you have no such experience, mark N/A.

09. Describe your experience in coordinating compliance with ADA, Section 504, Section 508, California Title 5, WCAG, or similar accessibility requirements. In your response, indicate (a) the organization(s) where you gained this experience, (b) the dates of employment, and (c) provide a summary of your duties/responsibilities regarding ADA and accessibility compliance. If you have no such experience, mark N/A.

10. Describe your experience in interpreting laws, regulations, or policies. In your response, indicate (a) the organization(s) where you gained this experience, (b) the dates of employment, and (c) provide a summary of your duties/responsibilities in interpreting laws, regulations and policies. If you have no such experience, mark N/A.

11. Describe your experience in conducting accessibility reviews, identifying compliance concerns, documenting findings, and monitoring corrective actions. In your response, indicate (a) the organization(s) where you gained this experience, (b) the dates of employment, and (c) provide an example of a time that you made a corrective action of an accessibility issue. If you have no such experience, mark N/A.

12. The testing process will require access to a computer with a camera, microphone, speakers, and a reliable connection to the internet. If you do not have access to one or more of these components and would like to request alternate testing accommodations, please indicate so below. Options: I do NOT have access to one or more of the required components and would like to request alternate testing accommodations. | I have access to ALL of the required components and do not need alternate testing accommodations.

A bachelor’s degree from a recognized college or university in public administration, business administration, human resources, law, education, disability studies, or a related field AND two years of experience coordinating compliance, programs, or projects of comparable complexity.

Coordinate activities to support districtwide compliance with ADA, CCR Title 5, Sections 504 and 508, and related accessibility regulations; ensure alignment with District policies, procedures, and legal requirements. E Monitor changes in federal and state laws, regulations, and guidance related to accessibility and disability compliance and applicable regulatory requirements; evaluate impacts, provide recommendations, and support implementation efforts. E Conduct districtwide accessibility reviews of programs, services, digital content, instructional materials, third-party tools, and facilities to identify barriers to access, areas of non-compliance, and potential compliance risks. E Coordinate, develop, and implement corrective action plans to address identified accessibility barriers; monitor progress and maintain documentation of compliance efforts. E Serve as a point of contact for accessibility-related complaints and inquiries; conduct intake of accessibility-related complaints and inquiries; create and maintain tracking systems to document, monitor, and follow through on cases; facilitate resolution through coordination with appropriate departments, as assigned. E Monitor and maintain accessibility-related grievance and appeal procedures, including case tracking, timelines, and documentation in accordance with established requirements; coordinate implementation and adherence to established processes. E Gather, review, and document information related to accessibility, disability access, and other compliance or human resources matters; coordinate documentation and logistics to support investigative or review processes, as assigned. E Serve as a resource to District departments on accessibility standards, compliance requirements, and procedural guidance; provide information, assistance, and training regarding available resources and best practices; coordinate with appropriate departments to support awareness and implementation of accessibility requirements. E Collaborate districtwide to support integration of accessibility requirements into programs and services; identify potential compliance issues and support integration of accessibility standards into procurement and implementation processes; provide guidance, in collaboration with Information Technology, on accessibility requirements for digital systems, software, web content, and third-party tools, including applicable state and federal standards. E Review and provide recommendations on proposed policies, procedures, programs, and projects to support alignment with accessibility laws and standards; review Board Policies and Administrative Procedures to ensure alignment with accessibility and disability compliance requirements and provide input to support identifying and recommending needed updates based on regulatory changes. E Review and provide input on facility design, alterations, and campus changes to support compliance with accessibility requirements. E Coordinate the collection and analysis of accessibility-related data; monitor and track required compliance reporting, documentation, and filings; prepare reports and summaries regarding accessibility compliance status, risk areas, and remediation progress for District leadership and external reporting requirements. E Coordinate and participate in committees, workgroups, and meetings related to accessibility, compliance, and equity initiatives. E Perform technical and administrative duties in support of District human resources, compliance, and related functions, as assigned. E Supervise, hire, train, and evaluate the performance of assigned employees; set performance requirements and goals; monitor and coach for improvement; promote excellence and customer service; take disciplinary action if needed according to District rules. E Work collaboratively and professionally with faculty, staff, students, and stakeholders from diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, and ethnic communities. E Demonstrate cultural humility, sensitivity, and equity-mindedness in working with individuals from diverse communities; model inclusive behaviors; and achieve equity in assignment-related outcomes. E Perform other duties as assigned. E = Essential duties.
